input.summary: iOS checkout conversion fell from about 0.060 to 0.028 at 08:00 on 2026-08-18 and reached 0.024 by 10:00 (expected about 0.057). The drop is broad: every country and every channel on iOS fell by roughly half. It began about 25 minutes after ios-7.3.0 (CHG-01188, redesigned payment sheet) rolled out to 100% at 07:35. Payment success by provider shows no single-provider failure. The earlier ios-2.42.7 release (21:33) preceded a stable period, so it does not fit. Not established: the mechanism inside the new payment sheet. Recommend rolling back ios-7.3.0.

PL card payment success fell from about 0.90 to 0.32 at 14:00 on 2026-08-05 and stayed low (0.35 at 15:00, 0.39 at 16:00) on about 20 attempts an hour. Other countries' card success is flat or up. The only PL card provider in the window is psp_beta, at 0.35 versus 0.91 baseline, pointing to a psp_beta failure in Poland. No change-log entry explains it; PL changes at 12:06 to 13:39 do not fit. I could not compare psp_beta with other providers, and no alternative was identified, so no failover is proposed. Confirm with the provider's status page.

ES web_mobile checkout conversion fell from about 13:00 on 2026-10-08: 2.4% at 13:00-14:00 against about 3.7% expected, and 3.4% at 15:00 against 4.0%. Sessions were only about 5-15% below expected. The drop is concentrated in ES: ES conversion over 13-16h was 2.7% against 4.3% baseline, while other countries were flat. Payment success by provider in ES showed no failing provider. The channel split is mixed. The change log has no ES web_mobile entry near 13:00; nearby entries (CDN cache config, storage and kids price changes, affiliate bid change) do not clearly fit. Cause not established; check the ES web_mobile checkout flow and tracking directly.

PL card payment success fell from about 0.90 to 0.32 at 14:00 UTC on 2026-08-05 and stayed low (0.35 at 15:00, 0.39 at 16:00) on roughly 20 attempts an hour. Other countries' card success is flat or up. The only provider visible for PL card in the window is psp_beta, at 0.35 versus 0.91 baseline, which points to a psp_beta failure in Poland. No change-log entry explains it: no provider status change was logged, and the PL-scoped changes were a price update and CDN config at 12:06 to 13:39, which do not fit. I could not compare psp_beta with other providers because the breakdown returned only psp_beta, and no alternative provider was identified, so no failover is proposed. Confirm with the provider's status page.

Web_desktop sessions ran about 5-11% above the same-hour expectation from 12:00 to 15:00 UTC on 2 Oct (peak 5818 vs 5263). The excess is spread across organic, direct and paid channels and across FR, DE and ES, with no single channel or country carrying it. Checkout conversion dipped to 0.054 vs 0.061 expected at 13:00 but recovered by 15:00. No calendar event and no change-log entry for web_desktop sits near the rise; the nearest web release (web-8.26.2) was 05:47, nine hours earlier. Bot traffic is not ruled out, but the spread across channels argues against it. Cause not established; the cause should be checked against traffic-source logs before any mitigation.

NL paid_search sessions rose from about 380 to 1,200-1,450 per hour starting 11:00 on 2026-09-24, against an expected 380-430. The rise is spread across all four platforms and is almost entirely NL; other countries are near baseline. Checkout conversion fell from about 5.4% to 1.7%, while implied orders stayed near the expected ~21 per hour. That fits bot or non-buying traffic rather than real demand. A feature-flags config change at 11:09 has no detail on its effect. The GARTEN15 coupon (12:14) came after onset, so it does not explain the start. I could not confirm the traffic source. No mitigation is proposed until verified.

Whole-business discount rate jumped from about 6.2% to about 16% starting exactly at 2026-08-28 00:00 and has stayed there through 08:00. The jump is uniform across all countries, channels and platforms, which matches the planned "Late summer weekend sale, all countries" (CAL-006, 28-31 Aug). No single slice stands out. The coupon VIP20 (created 05:56) and the web releases (06:08, 07:12, 08:38) all came after the onset, so they do not explain it. Not established: whether a sale should lift the discount rate this far, so the on-call should confirm the promotion's discount depth with the campaign owner. No mitigation proposed.

Paid_search sessions in NL jumped from about 400/hour to 1,200-1,450/hour starting around 10:00-11:00 UTC on 2026-09-24 (12:00: 1,446 vs expected 426). Checkout conversion fell from about 4.1% to 1.7% in the same hours. Other countries and channels in the window did not rise, so the surge is limited to NL paid search. No change-log entry concerns this slice, and no calendar event explains it. The pattern fits bot traffic, but I found no direct evidence of bots (no traffic-source or user-agent breakdown was available). Orders are not clearly unchanged, since they are slightly above expected. Confidence is medium, and I am not proposing a mitigation.

Gross margin has been below expected since 2026-08-28 00:00, not only since the alert hour. The discount rate stepped up from about 0.06 to about 0.16 at exactly that hour and has stayed there across all categories and countries. That matches the planned all-country "Late summer weekend sale" (CAL-006, 2026-08-28 to 2026-08-31). Discount-driven margin erosion explains the drop: on 08-30 at 11:00 margin was 0.343 against an expected 0.404. No coupon or price change in the log lines up with the step; VIP20 was created after it. This is a planned promotion, so no mitigation is proposed. The sale ends 2026-08-31 00:00, and margin should recover then. I did not verify the sale's own discount configuration.

PL card payment success fell from ~0.93-0.97 expected to 0.25-0.40 from 14:00 on 2026-08-05 and stayed low through 19:00. The drop sits entirely in provider psp_beta: in PL, psp_beta fell from 0.914 to 0.342 over 14:00-20:00, while psp_alpha, gamma, delta and epsilon held steady and psp_beta in ES and FR was flat or up. No provider_status change was logged, and the change log has no entry for psp_beta, so the trigger is unidentified. Recommend failover of PL card traffic away from psp_beta, pending confirmation with the provider. Web-6.7.0 (18:14) and SOMMER15 (18:56) do not match the PL-only, provider-specific pattern.

Gross margin rate has run about 7-8 points below expected since 2026-08-28 00:00 (0.338 vs 0.404 at alert hour). The drop is caused by discount rate rising from about 6% to about 16% starting at the same hour, uniformly across all six countries, all categories and all channels. Calendar shows planned promotion CAL-006 "Late summer weekend sale, all countries" starting 2026-08-28 00:00, which matches the onset and breadth. No concentrated slice, so no single-place fix. The VIP20 coupon (created 05:56) post-dates the onset and does not fit the uniform pattern. Not established: promotion discount depth was not verified against the promotion terms. Recommend confirming the sale is intended.

Recommend failing PL card traffic over from psp_beta, pending confirmation with the provider. Web-6.7.0 (18:14) and SOMMER15 (18:56) do not fit the PL-only, provider-specific pattern.

Garden gross margin in AT fell from about 0.43 to 0.10 over 08:00-12:00 on 2026-09-08 (11:00 hour at -0.15, below zero). Other AT categories are flat. Only garden-AT change in the window is CHG-01491, a manual price edit on GAR-51873 from 219.00 to 21.90 EUR at 08:40, a 90% cut that would sell below cost. Discount rate for garden-AT is not elevated, so a coupon is unlikely. Recommend pausing listing GAR-51873 and checking the price. Not established: exact order volume attributable to this SKU, since the data is not split by SKU.

Web_desktop sessions fell from about 4,800-5,000/hour to about 2,000/hour starting at 12:00 on 2026-10-01 and stayed there through 14:00. Other platforms are flat (web_mobile -2%, app_ios +2%, app_android -3%). Net revenue on web_desktop rose above expected over the same hours (12:00: 35,768 vs 29,246 expected), so orders did not drop. The only web_desktop change nearby is CHG-01830, a gtm-web container v231 publish with a new consent mode at 11:50, which fits a session-counting gap rather than a real traffic loss. Likely cause: tracking outage on desktop analytics, not a business drop. I did not verify the tag firing directly, and no mitigation applies to this cause.

PL card payment success fell from about 0.91 to 0.32 starting 14:00 on 2026-08-05 and was still at 0.39 at 16:00. The drop sits entirely on provider psp_beta: its success rate in PL over 14:00-17:00 was 0.35 against a 0.91 baseline, while psp_beta in ES and FR rose slightly. The change log has no provider_status or config entry for psp_beta or PL in the window, so the provider-side fault is inferred from the breakdown, not from a logged change. Cause within the provider is not established. Recommend failing PL card payments over from psp_beta, after checking the provider's status page.

Business-wide discount_rate ran above expected from about 10:00 to 13:00 on 2026-09-05 (e.g. 11:00 at 0.0640 vs 0.0612 expected; 13:00 at 0.0626 vs 0.0602), then returned to expected by 14:00 (0.0610 vs 0.0613). The excess is small and spread evenly across all six countries and all eight categories, so no single slice carries it. Change log entries before the rise (price updates FR textiles 09:42 and storage 11:32, tax-table config 09:46) do not plausibly raise discount rate. The KIDS10 usage-limit change at 13:12 started after the rise began and kids discount rate is not elevated. No coupon, campaign or calendar event clearly explains it. Cause not established; the breakdown baseline figures (~0.16) do not match the series baseline (~0.061), so that comparison was not usable. Recommend monitoring rather than a mitigation.

Sessions rose above expected from about 17:00 on 2026-10-15 (19:00: 26,044 observed vs 23,700 expected, about +10%). No calendar event and no change-log entry for traffic, campaigns or ES covers the period; the changes were price updates, search-ranking config and a tax-table config. I could not establish the source of the extra traffic and did not check conversion or orders. Suggest the on-call check ES traffic sources and referrals. No mitigation proposed.
